options.content:
### Keycloak troubleshooting dashboard (official, keycloak-grafana-dashboard@f819507c13, for Keycloak ≥ 26.3)
Upstream dashboard for the [Troubleshooting using metrics](https://www.keycloak.org/observability/metrics-for-troubleshooting)
guide; the day-to-day view is **Keycloak** (curated). Rows are collapsed: open the one you need. Lab: 1 replica with
**local** caches (`KC_CACHE=local`), so the upstream *Cluster Metrics* and *Clustered caching* rows (JGroups/replication)
and the CPU-vs-limit panel (no CPU limit set) were removed. Latency SLI and heatmap need the histogram options set in
`helm-charts/keycloak`. Docs: `docs/dashboards/security.md`.

panels.description: SLI: share of authentication requests with outcome SERVER_ERROR. Example SLO < 0.1 %.

panels.description: The percentage of CPU time spent on garbage collection, indicating the impact of GC on application performance in the JVM. It refers to the proportion of the total CPU processing time that is dedicated to executing garbage collection (GC) operations, as opposed to running application code or performing other tasks. This metric helps determine how much overhead GC introduces, affecting the overall performance of the Keycloak’s JVM.

panels.description:
Eviction is the process to limit the cache size and, when full, an entry is removed to make room for a new entry to be cached. As Keycloak caches the database entities in the users, realms and authorization, database access always proceeds with an eviction event.

A rapid increase of eviction and very high database CPU usage means the users or realms cache is too small for smooth Keycloak operation, as data needs to be re-loaded very often from the database which slows down responses. If enough memory is available, consider increasing the max cache size using the CLI options cache-embedded-users-max-count or cache-embedded-realms-max-count

targets.expr:
avg by (pod)((
irate(vendor_statistics_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_miss_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]))
/
(
    irate(vendor_statistics_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_miss_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m])
    + 
    irate(vendor_statistics_remove_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_remove_miss_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) 
    + 
    irate(vendor_statistics_store_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m])
))

panels.title: Read/Write ratio
panels.description: Reads divided by writes for the selected cache: a low ratio means the cache brings little.

panels.title: Average write operation time
panels.description: Average time of a cache write over the selected range.
A read operation reads a value from the cache. It divides into two groups, a hit if a value is found, and a miss if not found.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (irate(vendor_statistics_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_miss_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]))

targets.expr: avg by (pod)(irate(vendor_statistics_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", cache="$jdbc_cache_names", namespace="$namespace"}[5m]) / (irate(vendor_statistics_hit_times_seconds_count{cache="$jdbc_cache_names", namespace="$namespace", container="keycloak"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_miss_times_seconds_count{cache="$jdbc_cache_names", namespace="$namespace", container="keycloak"}[5m])))

panels.title: Cache read hit/miss ratio
panels.description: Share of cache reads that were hits. The troubleshooting guide flags a users cache hit ratio around 5 % as a cause of high latency (most lookups go to the database).
A read operation reads a value from the cache. It divides into two groups, a hit if a value is found, and a miss if not found.
panels.title: Number of cache read misses in 5 minute interval

panels.description: A remove operation removes a value from the cache. It divides in two groups, a hit if a value exists, and a miss if the value does not exist.

targets.expr: sum by (pod)(irate(vendor_statistics_remove_hit_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]) + irate(vendor_statistics_remove_miss_times_seconds_count{container="keycloak", namespace="$namespace", cache="$jdbc_cache_names"}[5m]))

panels.title: Number of remove operations in 5 minutes interval
